payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer m with m >= 2. For each h >= 0 let H_m(h)=|K_{m,h}|, and let
F_m(t)=\sum_{h=0}^\infty H_m(h)t^h
as a formal power series.

We must show that there exists a formal power series
G_m(t)=\sum_{h=0}^\infty c_h t^h
with each c_h \in \mathbf Z_{\ge 0} such that
(1-t)F_m(t)=H_m(0)+tG_m(t).

The key input is the trusted lemma stated in the shared context: for every integer g >= 0, there exists an injective map
J_{m,g}:K_{m,g}\to K_{m,g+1}.
Therefore, for every g >= 0,
|K_{m,g}| \le |K_{m,g+1}|,
that is,
H_m(g) \le H_m(g+1).
So for every h >= 0 the difference
c_h := H_m(h+1)-H_m(h)
is a well-defined nonnegative integer.

Now define
G_m(t):=\sum_{h=0}^\infty c_h t^h = \sum_{h=0}^\infty \bigl(H_m(h+1)-H_m(h)\bigr)t^h.
By construction each coefficient c_h lies in \mathbf Z_{\ge 0}.

It remains to verify the formal power series identity. Compute in the ring of formal power series:
\[
(1-t)F_m(t)=F_m(t)-tF_m(t).
\]
Since
\[
F_m(t)=\sum_{h=0}^\infty H_m(h)t^h,
\quad
tF_m(t)=\sum_{h=0}^\infty H_m(h)t^{h+1}=\sum_{n=1}^\infty H_m(n-1)t^n,
\]
we obtain by comparing coefficients that
\[
(1-t)F_m(t)=H_m(0)+\sum_{n=1}^\infty \bigl(H_m(n)-H_m(n-1)\bigr)t^n.
\]
Reindexing with h=n-1 gives
\[
(1-t)F_m(t)=H_m(0)+ t\sum_{h=0}^\infty \bigl(H_m(h+1)-H_m(h)\bigr)t^h
= H_m(0)+ tG_m(t).
\]
This is exactly the required form, and all coefficients of G_m(t) are nonnegative integers.

Hence such a formal power series G_m(t) exists.
payload.role_in_assembly: This is the main hard counting lemma: it packages the cardinality monotonicity into a positive Hilbert-series identity.

domain_restrictions: m is an integer with m ≥ 2
g is an integer with g ≥ 0
g + 1 is therefore an integer with g + 1 ≥ 1 (so the genus parameter remains in the intended nonnegative-integer regime)
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers m ≥ 2 and g ≥ 0, letting N(m,g) be the number of numerical semigroups having multiplicity m and genus g, we have N(m,g) ≤ N(m,g+1).

elements x of K_{m,h} satisfy x_i ∈ Z_{>0} for each i ∈ {1,...,m-1} (so in particular x_i are positive integers)

case condition for inequality 1: only imposed when i+j < m, and then uses index i+j ∈ {1,...,m-1}

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each fixed integer m ≥ 2, with K_{m,h} and H_m(h) defined as above and F_m(t)=Σ_{h=0}^∞ H_m(h)t^h, there exists a sequence (c_h)_{h≥0} with c_h ∈ Z_{≥0} such that, as formal power series, (1−t)F_m(t)=H_m(0)+ t Σ_{h=0}^∞ c_h t^h. Equivalently, for all n ≥ 1: c_{n-1} = H_m(n) − H_m(n−1), and each c_{n-1} is required to be a nonnegative integer.
quantifier_order: K_{m,h} consists of all x ∈ (Z_{>0})^{m-1} such that (sum_{k=1}^{m-1} x_k = h) and for all i,j ∈ {1,...,m-1} the inequalities hold with cases depending on whether i+j < m or i+j > m
there exists G_m(t) = Σ_{h=0}^∞ c_h t^h with c_h ∈ Z_{>=0} such that (1-t)F_m(t) = H_m(0) + t G_m(t)

payload.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2. For each integer h >= 0, define K_{m,h} to be the set of all tuples x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that x_1+...+x_{m-1}=h and such that for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i+j < m then x_i+x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i+j > m then x_i+x_j+1 >= x_{i+j-m}. Let H_m(h) be the number of elements of K_{m,h}, and define the formal power series F_m(t)=sum_{h=0}^infinity H_m(h) t^h. Then there exists a formal power series G_m(t)=sum_{h=0}^infinity c_h t^h with coefficients c_h in Z_{>=0} such that (1-t) F_m(t) = H_m(0) + t G_m(t).

detailed_findings.finding: The proof uses the trusted injectivity lemma exactly as intended to conclude H_m(g) ≤ H_m(g+1), yielding nonnegative integer differences c_h.
The formal power series manipulation is correct: (1-t)F_m(t) = H_m(0) + Σ_{n≥1}(H_m(n)-H_m(n-1)) t^n = H_m(0) + tG_m(t).
Finiteness of each H_m(h) is not explicitly justified before forming integer differences, though it is naturally true from the definition of K_{m,h} and consistent with the statement.

result_payload.reason: The proof correctly derives coefficientwise nonnegativity from the assumed injections J_{m,g}: K_{m,g} → K_{m,g+1}, defines c_h = H_m(h+1) - H_m(h), and verifies the formal power series identity by a standard coefficient computation. It matches the semantic sketch exactly and uses the intended monotonicity input. The only implicit point is finiteness of H_m(h), but this is already built into the statement's counting interpretation and is not a substantive gap in the argument.
